title: Bharati Station Surface Meteorology & Radiative Flux
content:
Continuous automatic weather station (AWS) observations deployed at Bharati Station (69°24′S, 76°11′E). Records 10-minute averaged air temperature, barometric pressure, horizontal wind velocity/direction, relative humidity, net radiation, and downward longwave/shortwave irradiance.
Variables: temp_surface (°C): Air temperature measured at 2m height; wind_speed (m/s): Horizontal wind speed at 10m height; pressure (hPa): Barometric station pressure; sw_down (W/m²): Downward shortwave solar radiation
Station: Bharati Station
Discipline: Atmospheric Sciences
Region: Antarctica

title: Ny-Ålesund Black Carbon & Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD)
content:
Ground-based aerosol characterization conducted during polar night and summer transition at Ny-Ålesund. Quantifies anthropogenic black carbon influx transported from mid-latitudes to the High Arctic and assesses snow albedo reduction.
Variables: bc_concentration (ng/m³): Equivalent black carbon mass concentration; aod_500nm (dimensionless): Aerosol Optical Depth at 500nm wavelength; pm25 (µg/m³): Fine particulate matter mass
Station: Himadri Station
Discipline: Atmospheric Sciences
Region: Arctic

title: Southern Ocean Hydrographic CTD Transect & Salinity Profile
content:
High-resolution oceanographic CTD rosette casts collected aboard research vessel along the 57.5°E transect. Captures water mass transformation, Antarctic Intermediate Water subduction, and Southern Ocean carbon sequestration pathways.
Variables: depth (dbar): Sea water pressure (equivalent depth); salinity (PSU): Practical Salinity Scale; sea_temp (°C): In-situ sea water temperature; oxygen (µmol/kg): Dissolved oxygen concentration
Station: Southern Ocean Survey
Discipline: Oceanography
Region: Southern Ocean

title: Chandra Basin High-Altitude Glacier Mass Balance & Runoff
content:
Long-term benchmark glaciological observations conducted from Himansh High-Altitude Research Station. Integrates stake network ablation rates, snow pits, dGPS terminal retreat mapping, and automatic river gauging to assess Third Pole freshwater vulnerability.
Variables: mass_balance (m w.e.): Annual specific glacier mass balance in meters water equivalent; ablation_rate (cm/day): Daily surface ice melt rate; discharge (m³/s): Proglacial stream discharge volume
Station: Himansh Station
Discipline: Glaciology & Cryosphere
Region: Himalayas

title: Maitri Station Deep Ice Core Stable Isotope Analysis (δ18O & δD)
content:
Isotopic ratios (Oxygen-18 and Deuterium) measured by cavity ring-down spectroscopy (CRDS) on firn and ice cores extracted near Maitri Station. Provides past atmospheric temperature records and teleconnections with the Indian Ocean Dipole.
Variables: d18o (‰): Oxygen-18 isotope delta value relative to VSMOW; dd (‰): Deuterium delta value relative to VSMOW; d_excess (‰): Deuterium excess (d = δD - 8*δ18O)
Station: Maitri Station
Discipline: Glaciology & Cryosphere
Region: Antarctica

title: Prydz Bay Marine Ecosystem & Phytoplankton Bloom Transect
content:
Biological oceanographic data investigating microbial biodiversity and primary productivity in sea-ice edge zones. Evaluates carbon export efficiency and ecological responses to changing fast-ice regimes.
Variables: chla (mg/m³): Active Chlorophyll-a fluorescence; nitrate (µmol/L): Dissolved inorganic nitrate concentration
Station: Prydz Bay Oceanographic Station
Discipline: Polar Biology & Ecosystems
Region: Antarctica

title: Kongsfjorden Fjord Hydrography & Marine Microbiology
content:
Continuous time-series from the IndARC subsurface mooring deployed at 192m water depth in Kongsfjorden. Tracks seasonal intrusion of warm Atlantic water into the inner fjord and its influence on Arctic marine ecosystem structure.
Variables: current_speed (cm/s): Acoustic Doppler current velocity; water_temp (°C): Subsurface water temperature; salinity (PSU): Mooring sensor salinity
Station: IndARC Mooring Observatory
Discipline: Oceanography
Region: Arctic

title: Siachen Glacier & Karakoram Ice Velocity Mapping via InSAR
content:
High-resolution surface velocity field and ice thickness estimates of Siachen Glacier. Investigates the Karakoram Anomaly through multi-temporal Sentinel-1 and ALOS-PALSAR radar interferometry validated with field benchmark dGPS surveys.
Variables: velocity (m/year): Surface ice displacement rate; elevation_change (m/year): Geodetic mass balance surface elevation trend
Station: Siachen Glacier Observatory
Discipline: Geology & Geophysics
Region: Himalayas

title: Understanding Antarctic Sea-Ice Dynamics and Global Climate Teleconnections
content:
A comprehensive investigation into the record minimums in Antarctic sea-ice extent and their direct teleconnection with Indian Summer Monsoon variability.

# Understanding Antarctic Sea-Ice Dynamics and Global Climate Teleconnections

**Author:** Dr. Thamban Meloth, National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research

## Abstract
Recent satellite microwave observations have revealed unprecedented winter and summer sea-ice loss in the Southern Ocean, particularly in the Weddell and Ross Sea sectors. This article synthesizes four decades of in-situ measurements from India's Maitri and Bharati stations...

## The Role of the Southern Annular Mode (SAM)
The Southern Annular Mode (SAM) has exhibited strongly positive phases, enhancing circumpolar westerly winds and driving warm deep water upwelling onto Antarctic continental shelves...

## Impacts on the Indian Summer Monsoon
Cross-equatorial atmospheric waves establish a teleconnection between Southern Ocean heat redistribution and the onset of the Southwest Monsoon over the Indian subcontinent.
Author: Dr. Thamban Meloth, NCPOR
Category: Climate & Cryosphere

title: Four Decades of India's Polar Research Programme: From Dakshin Gangotri to Bharati
content:
The monumental journey of Indian science in the polar regions, chronicling the establishment of Dakshin Gangotri, Maitri, Bharati, Himadri, and Himansh stations.

# Four Decades of India's Polar Research Programme: From Dakshin Gangotri to Bharati

India's Antarctic odyssey commenced in December 1981 under Operation Gangotri. Over the past 40 years, India has emerged as a frontline polar research nation under the Antarctic Treaty System...

## Station Infrastructure
1. **Dakshin Gangotri (1983):** India's first scientific camp.
2. **Maitri (1989):** Year-round inland hub in Schirmacher Oasis.
3. **Bharati (2012):** State-of-the-art modular station in Larsemann Hills.
4. **Himadri (2008):** High Arctic international station in Svalbard.
5. **Himansh (2016):** Third Pole high-altitude glaciological observatory.
Author: Dr. M. Ravichandran, MoES
Category: Expedition History

title: Black Carbon Transport to the High Arctic and Cryospheric Amplification
content:
Long-range airborne black carbon pollution transport pathways into Ny-Ålesund, Svalbard, and its accelerating impact on polar snow albedo feedback.

# Black Carbon Transport to the High Arctic and Cryospheric Amplification

Black carbon (BC) particles emitted from industrial combustion and wildfires at lower latitudes are transported across the circumpolar vortex into the High Arctic...

Observations from the Gruvebadet Atmospheric Laboratory and Himadri Station indicate substantial seasonal pulses during Arctic Haze episodes, darkening the snow cover and hastening springtime ablation.
Author: Dr. K. P. Krishnan, NCPOR
Category: Atmospheric Sciences

title: Himalayan Cryosphere under a Warming Climate: Observations from Himansh
content:
Decadal glaciological mass balance and ice velocity tracking from Chandra Basin benchmark glaciers in Himachal Pradesh.

# Himalayan Cryosphere under a Warming Climate: Observations from Himansh

The Hindu Kush Himalayas, known as Earth's Third Pole, store the largest volume of ice outside the polar regions. Data collected from the Himansh Observatory at 4,080m reveals persistent negative mass balances across Chandra basin glaciers...

Continuous discharge monitoring indicates elevated meltwater runoff in early summer followed by reduced late-season flow, posing challenges for river basin water management.
Author: Dr. Parmanand Sharma, NCPOR
Category: Glaciology

title: Biogeochemical Cycles and Carbon Sequestration in the Southern Ocean
content:
Quantifying the Southern Ocean biological carbon pump and Southern Annular Mode-driven iron fertilization mechanisms.

# Biogeochemical Cycles and Carbon Sequestration in the Southern Ocean

The Southern Ocean accounts for nearly 40% of the anthropogenic carbon dioxide absorbed by the global oceans. Scientific cruises under the Indian Southern Ocean Expedition have mapped nutrient limitation and phytoplankton blooms across the Polar Front.
Author: Dr. N. Anilkumar, NCPOR
Category: Oceanography

title: Albedo
content:
Simple Definition: How well a surface reflects sunlight. Fresh white snow has high albedo (reflects up to 90% of heat), while dark open ocean has low albedo (absorbs heat).
Scientific Definition: The non-dimensional measure of diffuse reflectivity of solar radiation out of the total incident solar irradiance across the planetary surface.
Category: Cryospheric Physics

title: Katabatic Winds
content:
Simple Definition: Extremely fierce, cold winds that rush down high Antarctic ice slopes toward the coast under the pull of gravity, often exceeding 100 km/h.
Scientific Definition: Gravity-driven downslope drainage flows of dense, radiatively cooled boundary-layer air originating over the high Antarctic plateau.
Category: Polar Meteorology

title: Polynya
content:
Simple Definition: An open patch of water in the middle of frozen sea ice where sea animals like penguins and seals can surface to breathe.
Scientific Definition: Non-linear open water regions within sea ice pack sustained either by sensible heat upwelling or latent heat divergence driven by offshore winds.
Category: Oceanography & Sea Ice

title: Ice Shelf
content:
Simple Definition: A massive floating slab of permanent ice that extends from land over the ocean. When they break off, they form giant tabular icebergs.
Scientific Definition: A thick, buoyant platform of meteoric ice fed by grounding tributary glaciers that extends into a marine or lacustrine embayment.
Category: Glaciology

title: Black Carbon
content:
Simple Definition: Dark soot particles released from fires and vehicle exhaust that drift across the air to the Arctic and darken snow, causing it to melt faster.
Scientific Definition: A primary component of fine particulate matter (PM2.5) consisting of pure carbon formed through incomplete combustion of fossil fuels, biofuels, and biomass.
Category: Atmospheric Sciences

title: Antarctic Bottom Water (AABW) Subduction
content:
Simple Definition: The process where surface water in Antarctica gets super cold and salty, sinks to the deep ocean floor, and powers global ocean currents.
Scientific Definition: Densification and deep sinking of hypersaline shelf brine driving the lower limb of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC).
Category: Ocean Circulation
